description: A lowpass filter built as an unstable feedback loop with non-linearity in it, made to be swept, overdriven or struck like a drum

params.text: Sets the base frequency of the filter, and with it the pitch of the drum when the filter is pinged
Sets how much of the filter's own state is fed back into its velocity; near the top of its travel the ringing sustains, and this is what sets the decay when the filter is used as a drum
Feeds the filter's output back into its input, which pulls the frequency down and changes the timbre; struck, it gives a downward sweep from the base pitch
Bends the filter frequency by the filter's own output, so the frequency flutters in step with the sound passing through; none at the far left
Sets the gain into the filter, from an eighth at the far left through unity at centre to eight times at the far right, which drives the internal soft clipper and dirties the sound
Sets how much modulation reaches the frequency: turned clockwise of centre it scales the positive modulation input, and anticlockwise of centre it scales the negative one
Sets how much modulation reaches the resonance: turned clockwise of centre it scales the positive modulation input, and anticlockwise of centre it scales the negative one
Sets how much modulation reaches the feedback: turned clockwise of centre it scales the positive modulation input, and anticlockwise of centre it scales the negative one
Sets how much modulation reaches the radioactivity: turned clockwise of centre it scales the positive modulation input, and anticlockwise of centre it scales the negative one
Sets how much modulation reaches the gain: turned clockwise of centre it scales the positive modulation input, and anticlockwise of centre it scales the negative one
Chooses how the negative modulation input is treated when it is empty and takes its reading from the positive one: in one position it arrives as it stands and in the other it arrives inverted

inputs.text: The audio to be filtered, or the click to ping the filter with; nothing happens at either output until something is patched here
The positive modulation input for the five attenuverters down the left of the panel
The negative modulation input for those same five attenuverters; with nothing patched it reads the positive input

outputs.text: The lowpassed audio, soft clipped at 7V
What is left of the input after the lowpassed part and the feedback are taken out of it, soft clipped at 7V

notes: The channel count of everything is taken from the audio input alone, so with that jack empty the module runs no code at all and the modulation inputs do nothing
menu: Use Classic Theme — returns the panel to the original untinted artwork, which no entry in the Panel Theme list will give back
